name: Cartesia
positioning: Cartesia offers the Sonic family of streaming text-to-speech models, plus speech-to-text and managed voice agents, aimed at real-time conversational use.

pricing.model: Monthly subscription that includes a pool of credits (1 credit is about 1 TTS character), with optional per-credit overage billing.
pricing.headline: Pro plan: $5/month for 100K credits, an effective $50 per 1M characters; larger plans lower the effective rate to about $37 per 1M.
pricing.headlineTier: Pro plan, Sonic-3.6 (effective rate: $5 / 100K credits; first paid plan with commercial license)

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Evaluation and personal use; no commercial license listed on the plan card.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.notes: Derived: 5/100000*1e6. Includes commercial use license and instant voice cloning. Overage $65 per 1M credits if enabled.

tiers.name: Startup
tiers.notes: Derived: 49/1.25. Adds professional voice cloning (2 slots). Overage $45 per 1M credits.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.notes: Derived: 299/8, rounded. 4 PVC slots, priority support, higher concurrency. Overage $38 per 1M credits.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Volume pricing; BAAs/DPAs, SSO, custom concurrency.

pricing.freeTier: 20K credits per month (about 20K characters of Sonic TTS), 2 concurrent TTS requests.
promotions: Managed Agent evaluations and LLM usage for UI-created agents are free 'for a limited time' (no end date stated); not relevant to TTS API pricing.

voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Instant voice cloning from a short clip (Pro and above); professional voice cloning on Startup and above; clones require verified consent.

streaming.vendorStatedLatency: Vendor-stated: first audio in under 90 ms (model latency), 'sub-90ms'. Not independently measured.

compatibility.note: Cartesia documents its own /tts/bytes, /tts/sse and /tts/websocket endpoints with a different request shape (model_id, transcript, voice, output_format); no OpenAI-style /v1/audio/speech route was found in the pages read.

licensing.commercialUse: Commercial use license is listed from the Pro plan upward; the Free plan is described as for evaluation and personal use.
licensing.attributionOrConditions: Voice clones need verified consent; cloning people without permission is prohibited by the Terms of Use (vendor-stated).

limits.concurrency: TTS concurrent requests by plan: Free 2, Pro 3, Startup 5, Scale 15, Enterprise custom. Exceeding returns 429.

compliance.note: Self-attested on the Sonic product page: SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA-eligible with BAAs, GDPR; BAAs/DPAs on the Enterprise plan. Zero data retention is described as available for enterprise customers.

strengths.claim: Vendor states Sonic delivers first audio in under 90 ms (vendor-stated, not independently verified).
Sonic 3.6 supports 44 languages from one model.
Offers instant and professional voice cloning plus an SSML-like tag set for speed, volume and emotion.
Publishes SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA-eligibility with BAAs, and GDPR statements, with on-prem/VPC deployment for enterprise.
Failed requests do not consume credits; official Python and JavaScript SDKs and LiveKit/Pipecat integrations.

limitations.claim: Billing is a monthly subscription with a credit pool; Pro's effective rate is $50 per 1M characters and overage rates are $38 to $65 per 1M credits depending on plan.
Free-plan concurrency is 2 TTS requests and Pro is 3; higher concurrency requires Startup or above.

stepsToMove: Replace POST /tts/bytes (or /tts/sse or /tts/websocket) with ReadAloud's speech endpoint (OpenAI-style or ElevenLabs-style route).
Map Cartesia's 'transcript' field to the input text field and 'model_id' (e.g. sonic-3.6) to a ReadAloud model or tier.
Replace the Cartesia voice UUID in 'voice' with a ReadAloud voice name.
Swap 'output_format' (container wav/mp3/raw plus encoding and sample_rate) for ReadAloud's response format setting.
Replace the Bearer sk_car_ API key and Cartesia-Version header with the ReadAloud key.
Convert any Cartesia SSML tags (speed, volume, break) or generation_config to supported ReadAloud controls, or remove them.
Cloned voices and Cartesia-specific voice IDs do not carry over.

bestFor: Teams building real-time voice agents or multilingual products who want a low-latency model with broad language coverage, cloning options and published compliance statements, and who are comfortable with a credit-based subscription.

sources.title: Cartesia docs: Concurrency and WebSocket limits

unknowns: Total number of voices in the voice library
SSML support is a Cartesia-specific tag subset (speed, volume, break/emotion), not full W3C SSML
Whether any OpenAI-compatible speech route exists
Credit use is 'approximately' 1 per character and may vary slightly with pre-processing

Plan prices and credit allotments are single-source (cartesia.ai/pricing); the docs pricing page confirms only the ~1 credit per character rate. Per-1M figures are derived by dividing plan price by credits
